title: Sporting · gundogs
blurb: The shooting dogs of Britain and the continent: pointers that freeze, setters that range, spaniels that flush and retrievers that bring it back.

items.d: Newfoundland water dog refined in Britain: 25–36 kg, the world's commonest gundog and assistance dog.
Scottish shooting dog of the 1860s, bred to retrieve from water and land and now a guide dog.
English flushing spaniel that springs game from cover; 19–25 kg, busy and biddable.
The smaller English spaniel, named for woodcock: 12–15 kg, with a feathered coat and a wagging tail.
Long-coated pointing dog of four hundred years' standing, working the moor with a crouching set.
The red setter of Ireland: 25–32 kg, far-ranging, and slower to mature than most gundogs.
German pointing dog from Weimar's court, 25–40 kg, with a silver-grey coat and no fear.
French pointing dog with a naturally short tail, 14–20 kg, and a tireless, close-working quarter.
